faq: Which platforms can you move from?
Wix, Squarespace, Shopify pages, Webflow, Weebly, Joomla, Drupal and plain HTML sites are common. Send the link and we confirm what can move and what must be rebuilt.
Will I lose my Google rankings?
We cannot promise rankings, but we copy titles and descriptions and set 301 redirects so search engines can follow your old links. A clean move keeps most of your search visibility.
Do I need to cancel my old site first?
No, keep it live until the new site is approved. Cancel it only after launch, and we tell you when it is safe so nothing breaks while you switch the domain.
Can you move an online store?
This service is for content sites. For stores with products and orders, choose our WooCommerce migration, which carries products, customers and orders.

desc:
Moving a website to a new platform is easy to start and easy to get wrong. Ecom Swift LLC helps you migrate your website to WordPress with pages, posts, images and redirects carried across, tested on a private copy before launch.

## What does it mean to migrate your website to WordPress?

Migrating to WordPress means moving your content, structure and address from another platform, such as Wix, Squarespace or Shopify, into a WordPress site that you control. It covers pages, blog posts, images, menus, forms and the links that other sites and search engines already use.

A good migration is quiet. Visitors reach the same content at the same addresses, or are sent to the new ones automatically.

## Why migrations go wrong

Most problems come from what is not copied. Images stay on the old platform and disappear when the plan ends. Menus are rebuilt differently, so pages become hard to find. Old addresses stop working, and every link from other sites, social posts and search results leads to an error page.

Another risk is timing. If the domain is switched before the new site is ready, visitors see a half-built page. A planned migration separates the build from the launch, so you decide when the switch happens.

## How migration affects your site's performance

Redirects are the key. When an old address points to its new equivalent, visitors and search engines follow the path and land on the right page. Without redirects, links stop working and the work you put into your content and visibility is lost.

Moving to WordPress also gives you control over hosting, themes and plugins, which can help speed and flexibility. We cannot promise that rankings stay exactly the same, since a platform change, new layout and timing all play a part. A careful move reduces the risk.

## What a careful migration includes

- A full inventory of existing pages, posts, images and menus.
- Content copied into WordPress with headings, formatting and image placement intact.
- Blog categories, tags and authors kept where the platform allows.
- A clean theme set up with your logo, colors and fonts.
- Forms rebuilt and tested so messages reach you.
- Page titles and descriptions copied across.
- A redirect map linking each old address to its new page.
- A private preview for your approval before launch.
- Checks on domain and email settings before the switch.
- A link check after launch, to catch what was missed.

## How we handle the move

We start with a list of what exists on your current site. We build the WordPress site on a private address, move the content and rebuild the layout. You review the preview and tell us what to change.

When you approve, we help you choose the moment to launch. We guide the domain changes, set the redirects and check email routing, because mail often depends on the same domain. Basic suits a small site. Standard handles more pages, posts, forms and a redirect map. Premium covers a larger site with a layout rebuild, speed settings and a link check after launch. Add-ons cover extra posts, image clean-up and an email setup check.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep your old site live until the new one is approved.
- Export a backup of everything you have today.
- List the pages that bring you the most visitors.
- Send a test message to your business address once the domain points to the new site.
- Review the new site on a phone and a computer.

**Avoid:**
- Cancelling your old plan before launch.
- Changing page addresses without redirects.
- Rebuilding the design and the content structure at the same time without a plan.
- Leaving images hosted on the old platform.
- Launching late on a Friday when nobody can check.

## Who it is for

Small business owners who have outgrown a website builder and want more control are a common fit. Bloggers and publishers who want their archive in WordPress will also benefit. So will anyone who wants to bring several older sites into one place without losing their links.

## How to get started

Send the address of your current site, the platform it runs on and the pages you consider most important. We never ask for passwords. We use a collaborator, staff or developer invitation on your old platform and your new hosting, which you can remove afterwards. Online stores need a separate conversation, because products and orders are handled differently from pages.
